claims.text: The starting AlCoCrFeNi2.1 alloy has a uniform, fine lamellar eutectic microstructure.
The starting alloy has strength and plasticity below industrial fastener requirements.
The proposed intervention is post-solidification aging at approximately 700 °C for approximately 10 hours in an inert atmosphere, followed by controlled cooling.
The proposed aging treatment will promote nucleation and growth of nanoscale secondary precipitates.
The nanoscale precipitates will form preferentially at lamellar interfaces.
The precipitates will obstruct dislocation motion through precipitation strengthening.
The interfacial precipitates will stabilize the lamellar interfaces.
The precipitates and stabilized interfaces will retard diffusion-controlled creep processes.
Precipitate-induced changes in interfacial chemistry may reduce localized corrosion initiation.
Aging will increase yield strength relative to the untreated starting alloy.
Aging will improve room-temperature creep resistance relative to the untreated starting alloy.
Aging will maintain or modestly enhance plasticity relative to the untreated starting alloy.
Aging will improve corrosion endurance relative to the untreated starting alloy.
The aged alloy will perform better under thermal cycling from approximately -50 °C to 300 °C.
The anticipated benefit applies under prolonged room-temperature mechanical loading.
The anticipated benefit applies in moderately corrosive environments such as salt spray.
Outside the stated thermal, loading, and corrosion limits, the benefits may diminish or require additional interventions.
Precipitation strengthening is a well-established mechanism.

contradictions.description: The main hypothesis says plasticity will improve, whereas the predicted outcome allows plasticity merely to be maintained. Maintenance does not establish the claimed concurrent improvement.
